AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To investigate patients' expectations of lingual orthodontic treatment.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: In-depth interviews were conducted. A framework analysis was carried out to identify themes, concepts and a typology.

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: Two secondary care hospital departments and four primary care orthodontic practices, UK.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: Fifteen new orthodontic patients aged 16-60 years participated in the interviews. All interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed using framework analysis, including identification of themes within the responses, and typologies of respondents.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Patients seeking lingual orthodontics reported expectations that were similar in quality but different in extent to those seeking labial orthodontics. These patients were well informed about lingual orthodontic treatment before they decide to start treatment. Two typologies were identified. Firstly, males less than 30 years of age, undergoing changes in their lives, who were confident that they wanted a hidden brace, but were not entirely sure of the specifics of the system. Secondly, females aged 30-45, who request a hidden brace and had actively researched what particular systems were available.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: This study shows that patients requesting lingual orthodontics have expectations that are similar in quality but greater in extent when compared to those seeking labial orthodontics.
